ex.en: The doctor continued to observe the patient's behavior.
ex.zh: 醫生繼續觀察病人的一舉一動。

ex.en: The lonely man derives pleasure from observing ants.
ex.zh: 那個孤僻的人以觀察螞蟻為樂。

ex.en: The woman observes and the man thinks.
ex.zh: 女人觀察，男人思考。

observe.en: to watch someone or something carefully

ex.en: He observed that we should probably have rain coming.
ex.zh: 他說大概快下雨了。

ex.en: "It's getting late," she observed.
ex.zh: 「時間不早了。」她說。

observe.en: to say something about what you have noticed

ex.en: All drivers must observe the speed limit.
ex.zh: 所有駕駛都必須遵守速限。

ex.en: Many families still observe this tradition.
ex.zh: 許多家庭仍然遵守這個傳統。

observe.en: to obey a rule or follow a custom

ex.en: I am able to obtain a registration form for free.
ex.zh: 我可以免費索取報名表。

ex.en: It is necessary to obtain the sanction of the authorities to enter this building.
ex.zh: 要進入這棟大樓，必須取得有關當局的許可。

ex.en: They obtained a yield of 8 percent on their investment.
ex.zh: 他們的投資獲得了百分之八的報酬。

obtain.en: to get something, often by effort

obligate.zh: 使負有義務（常用 be obligated to）

ex.en: I felt obligated.
ex.zh: 我覺得有義務這麼做。

ex.en: Employees are obligated to follow the safety rules.
ex.zh: 員工有義務遵守安全規定。

obligate.en: to make someone feel they must do something

oblige.zh: 迫使（be obliged to 不得不、有義務）

ex.en: She was obliged to give up the plan.
ex.zh: 她不得不放棄那個計畫。

ex.en: We're not obliged to do that for Tom.
ex.zh: 我們沒有義務替湯姆做那件事。

ex.en: The train was so crowded that we were obliged to stand all the way to Osaka.
ex.zh: 火車太擠了，我們只好一路站到大阪。

oblige.en: to force someone to do something because of a rule or duty

oblige.zh: 幫忙、答應（請求）；（much obliged）非常感激

ex.en: I'd be happy to oblige if you need any help.
ex.zh: 如果你需要幫忙，我很樂意效勞。

ex.en: I'm much obliged to you for your help.
ex.zh: 非常感謝你的幫忙。

oblige.en: to help someone by doing what they ask

ex.en: Observers expect prices to fall next year.
ex.zh: 觀察人士預期明年價格會下跌。

ex.en: She attended the meeting as an observer.
ex.zh: 她以觀察員身分出席會議。

observer.en: a person who watches and studies events

ex.en: Tom was the biggest obstacle for them.
ex.zh: 湯姆是他們最大的阻礙。

ex.en: He can overcome any obstacle.
ex.zh: 他能克服任何障礙。

ex.en: Bats use ultrasound to locate obstacles.
ex.zh: 蝙蝠利用超音波來找出障礙物的位置。

obstacle.en: something that blocks your way or makes progress difficult

ex.en: I read his obituary in the newspaper.
ex.zh: 我在報紙上看到他的訃聞。

ex.en: The obituary described her as a kind teacher.
ex.zh: 訃聞形容她是一位親切的老師。

obituary.en: a notice in a newspaper about a person who has died

ex.en: The meaning of this sentence is obscure.
ex.zh: 這個句子的意思很模糊。

ex.en: The instructions were written in obscure language.
ex.zh: 說明書的用語很難懂。

obscure.en: not clear and hard to understand

ex.en: He was an obscure writer before he won the prize.
ex.zh: 他得獎前是個沒沒無聞的作家。

ex.en: The song was written by an obscure band.
ex.zh: 這首歌是一個不知名的樂團寫的。

ex.en: Clouds obscured our view of the mountain.
ex.zh: 雲遮住了我們看山的視線。

ex.en: The report obscures the real problems.
ex.zh: 這份報告掩蓋了真正的問題。

obscure.en: to make something hard to see or understand

ex.en: Tom is obviously going to need more help.
ex.zh: 湯姆顯然會需要更多幫助。

ex.en: This drink's flavor is obviously that of tea.
ex.zh: 這個飲料喝起來明顯是茶的味道。

ex.en: He can speak French, and obviously English.
ex.zh: 他會說法語，英語當然也會。

obviously.en: in a way that is easy to see or understand

ex.en: The house was full of colorful art objects.
ex.zh: 房子裡擺滿了色彩繽紛的藝術品。

ex.en: Do not leave any objects on the stairs.
ex.zh: 不要把任何物品留在樓梯上。

object.en: a thing that you can see or touch

ex.en: His main object in life was to become rich.
ex.zh: 他人生的主要目標是成為有錢人。

ex.en: The object of the game is to score points.
ex.zh: 這個遊戲的目標是得分。

object.en: the aim or purpose of an action

ex.en: He objects to being treated like a child.
ex.zh: 他不喜歡被當成小孩對待。

ex.en: I objected to his paying the bill.
ex.zh: 我反對讓他付帳。

ex.en: He objected to his wife working outside.
ex.zh: 他反對妻子在外工作。

object.en: to say that you do not agree with or like something

ex.en: It was obvious that they had told a lie.
ex.zh: 很明顯他們說了謊。

ex.en: It's so obvious we don't need proof.
ex.zh: 事情這麼明顯，根本不需要證據。

ex.en: It seems obvious that he is sick.
ex.zh: 他顯然是生病了。

ex.en: Her acute observation skills make her a very suitable photographer.
ex.zh: 她敏銳的觀察力讓她很適合當攝影師。

ex.en: His observations are sharp, but he doesn't say much.
ex.zh: 他的觀察很敏銳，但話不多。

ex.en: The patient was kept under observation overnight.
ex.zh: 病人留院觀察了一晚。

observation.en: the act of watching something carefully, or the ability to do it

ex.en: Let me make a few observations about the report.
ex.zh: 讓我針對這份報告提出幾點看法。

ex.en: She made an interesting observation about the market.
ex.zh: 她對市場提出了一個很有意思的見解。

observation.en: a comment about something you have noticed

ex.en: Every player is under obligation to keep the rules.
ex.zh: 每位選手都有義務遵守規則。

ex.en: I actually don't have an obligation to help you.
ex.zh: 其實我沒有義務幫你。

ex.en: It is our obligation to help.
ex.zh: 幫忙是我們的義務。

obligation.en: something you must do because of a law, promise, or duty

ex.en: A large pillar obstructs the view of the lake.
ex.zh: 巨大的柱子遮住了視線，讓人看不到湖。

ex.en: A fallen tree obstructed the road.
ex.zh: 有棵樹倒了下來，把路堵住了。

ex.en: The crowd obstructed the police in the discharge of their duties.
ex.zh: 群眾妨礙了警員執行任務。

obstruct.en: to block a path or view, or to make progress difficult

ex.en: Ghosts and gods are the obsessions of the human world.
ex.zh: 鬼神是人世間的執念。

ex.en: Her obsession with cleanliness affects her daily life.
ex.zh: 她對清潔的執著影響了她的日常生活。

ex.en: Fame has become an obsession for him.
ex.zh: 名氣已成為他念念不忘的執念。

obsession.en: a thought or interest that fills your mind all the time

ex.en: I have been obsessed with French recently.
ex.zh: 我最近著迷於法語。

ex.en: Carl, you're obsessed with money.
ex.zh: Carl，你被錢迷住了。

ex.en: He is obsessed with baseball.
ex.zh: 他對棒球著了迷。

obsessed.en: thinking about one thing all the time

obscene.zh: 猥褻的、淫穢的、令人厭惡的

ex.en: One must be respectful when speaking, and not say obscene things.
ex.zh: 開口要有禮貌，不講下流話。

ex.en: The film was banned for its obscene content.
ex.zh: 這部電影因內容猥褻而被禁演。

ex.en: He was fined for making obscene gestures at the referee.
ex.zh: 他因對裁判做出下流手勢而被罰款。

obscene.en: shocking and offensive, especially in a sexual way (offensive)

ex.en: He was oblivious to the problems in his team.
ex.zh: 他完全沒察覺到團隊裡的問題。

ex.en: She walked on, oblivious of the rain.
ex.zh: 她繼續往前走，渾然不覺下雨了。

oblivious.en: not aware of what is happening around you

ex.en: My grandfather remained obdurate and refused to see a doctor.
ex.zh: 我爺爺依然很固執，拒絕去看醫生。

ex.en: The manager was obdurate and would not change his decision.
ex.zh: 經理態度強硬，不肯改變他的決定。

obdurate.en: refusing to change your mind or actions

ex.en: He was a great teacher so his children were very obedient.
ex.zh: 他很會教孩子，所以他的孩子都很聽話。

ex.en: When you go to play at a friend's house, you need to be well behaved and obedient.
ex.zh: 你去朋友家玩的時候要守規矩、要聽話。

ex.en: Our dog is very obedient and always comes when called.
ex.zh: 我們的狗很聽話，一叫就會過來。

obedient.en: doing what you are told to do

ex.en: The company replaced its obsolete billing system.
ex.zh: 公司汰換了過時的帳務系統。

ex.en: These parts are obsolete and hard to find.
ex.zh: 這些零件已經停產，很難找到。

obsolete.en: no longer used because something newer is better

ex.en: Rapid obsolescence makes regular upgrades necessary.
ex.zh: 快速淘汰使定期升級變得必要。

ex.en: The design reduces the risk of early obsolescence.
ex.zh: 這項設計降低了產品提早過時的風險。

obsolescence.en: the process of becoming old and no longer used

ex.en: The report examines how sleep affects childhood obesity.
ex.zh: 這份報告探討睡眠如何影響兒童肥胖問題。

ex.en: The program addresses obesity through nutrition education and exercise.
ex.zh: 這項計畫透過營養教育和運動處理肥胖問題。

obesity.en: the condition of being very overweight in a way that harms health

ex.en: In the end he achieved his objective.
ex.zh: 他終於完成了他的目標。

ex.en: He explained the plan's main objective.
ex.zh: 他解釋了這個計劃的主要目標。

ex.en: The objectives of the marketing department and the sales department are not necessarily the same.
ex.zh: 行銷部和業務部的目標不見得相同。

objective.en: something you are trying to achieve

ex.en: It's hard to stay objective and calm when it happens to you.
ex.zh: 事情發生在自己身上時，很難保持客觀冷靜。

ex.en: Does objective history exist?
ex.zh: 客觀的歷史存在嗎？

objective.en: based on facts and not on personal feelings

ex.en: I have no objection to your plan.
ex.zh: 我不反對你的計劃。

ex.en: She has a strong objection to my plan.
ex.zh: 她強烈反對我的計劃。

ex.en: If Tom wants to stay, I have no objection.
ex.zh: 如果湯姆想留下來，我沒有意見。

objection.en: a statement that you do not agree with or like something

ex.en: I felt obliged to help my neighbor.
ex.zh: 我覺得有義務幫助我的鄰居。

ex.en: Drivers are obliged to stop at a red light.
ex.zh: 駕駛人必須在紅燈時停車。

ex.en: I am much obliged to you for your help.
ex.zh: 非常感謝你的幫忙。

ex.en: We were obliged for the kind invitation.
ex.zh: 我們很感激這次親切的邀請。

ex.en: Children should obey their parents and teachers.
ex.zh: 孩子應該聽從父母和老師的話。

ex.en: All drivers must obey the traffic rules.
ex.zh: 所有駕駛人都必須遵守交通規則。

ex.en: A fallen tree caused an obstruction on the road.
ex.zh: 一棵倒下的樹擋住了道路。

ex.en: Please remove any obstruction from the exit.
ex.zh: 請清除出口處的任何障礙物。

ex.en: The doctor found an obstruction in his airway.
ex.zh: 醫生發現他的呼吸道有阻塞。

ex.en: He was accused of obstruction of justice.
ex.zh: 他被控妨礙司法公正。

ex.en: The dog showed perfect obedience to its owner.
ex.zh: 那隻狗對主人表現出完全的服從。

ex.en: Soldiers are trained to follow orders with strict obedience.
ex.zh: 士兵受訓要嚴格服從命令。

ex.en: We visited the observatory to look at the stars.
ex.zh: 我們去天文臺看星星。

ex.en: The observatory sits on top of a quiet mountain.
ex.zh: 天文臺位於一座寧靜的山頂上。

ex.en: A good judge must keep objectivity in every case.
ex.zh: 好的法官在每個案件中都必須保持客觀。

ex.en: Journalists are trained to report with objectivity.
ex.zh: 記者受過訓練，要客觀地報導。

ex.en: The scientist observed the birds for several weeks.
ex.zh: 那位科學家觀察了這些鳥好幾個星期。

ex.en: I observed that he was nervous before the test.
ex.zh: 我注意到他在考試前很緊張。

ex.en: Our family observed the holiday with a quiet dinner.
ex.zh: 我們家以一頓安靜的晚餐慶祝這個節日。

ex.en: The company has always observed the safety rules.
ex.zh: 這家公司一直遵守安全規定。

ex.en: He is obsessive about keeping his desk perfectly clean.
ex.zh: 他對保持桌面一塵不染到了執著的地步。

ex.en: Her obsessive interest in the singer worried her parents.
ex.zh: 她對那位歌手近乎著迷的熱衷讓父母很擔心。

ex.en: He washes his hands in an obsessive way, even when they are clean.
ex.zh: 他即使雙手很乾淨，還是會強迫性地洗手。

ex.en: Obsessive thoughts kept her awake all night.
ex.zh: 揮之不去的強迫性念頭讓她整晚睡不著。

ex.en: Doctors warn that obese people have a higher risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 醫生警告說，肥胖的人罹患心臟病的風險較高。

ex.en: The dog became obese because it ate too many treats.
ex.zh: 那隻狗因為吃太多零食而變得過胖。

ex.en: The heavy rain obliterated the footprints on the beach.
ex.zh: 大雨把沙灘上的腳印沖刷得無影無蹤。

ex.en: He tried to obliterate the memory of that awful night.
ex.zh: 他試圖抹去那個可怕夜晚的記憶。

ex.en: The storm threatened to obliterate the small village.
ex.zh: 這場風暴有可能把小村莊夷為平地。

ex.en: It is hard to judge your own work objectively.
ex.zh: 要客觀地評價自己的作品很難。

ex.en: Try to look at the facts objectively before deciding.
ex.zh: 做決定前，試著客觀地看待事實。

ex.en: The poet lived and died in obscurity.
ex.zh: 那位詩人默默無聞地過完一生。

ex.en: The band rose from obscurity to fame in a year.
ex.zh: 這個樂團一年內從默默無名變得家喻戶曉。

ex.en: The obscurity of the legal language confused me.
ex.zh: 法律用語的艱澀讓我一頭霧水。

ex.en: Critics complained about the obscurity of the poem.
ex.zh: 評論家抱怨那首詩晦澀難懂。

ex.en: The tickets are obtainable at the front desk.
ex.zh: 票可以在櫃台取得。

ex.en: Fresh vegetables are easily obtainable in this area.
ex.zh: 這個地區很容易買到新鮮蔬菜。

ex.en: The old singer faded into oblivion.
ex.zh: 那位老歌手逐漸被世人遺忘。

ex.en: After the long day, he drank tea and sank into blissful oblivion.
ex.zh: 漫長的一天後，他喝了茶，沉入忘我的睡意中。

ex.en: Wearing a helmet is obligatory on this bike path.
ex.zh: 在這條自行車道上必須戴安全帽。

ex.en: Attendance at the safety meeting is obligatory for all staff.
ex.zh: 所有員工都必須出席安全會議。

ex.en: The film was banned for obscenity.
ex.zh: 這部電影因猥褻而被禁演。

ex.en: The judge warned him not to shout obscenities in court.
ex.zh: 法官警告他不要在法庭上大喊粗話。

ex.en: Strict observance of the rules keeps everyone safe.
ex.zh: 嚴格遵守規則能讓每個人都安全。

ex.en: The observance of traffic laws is everyone's duty.
ex.zh: 遵守交通法規是每個人的責任。

ex.en: The town holds a quiet observance every year on that day.
ex.zh: 小鎮每年在那一天都會舉行一場安靜的紀念儀式。

ex.en: Religious observance is important to many families.
ex.zh: 宗教儀式對許多家庭來說很重要。

ex.en: The change in temperature is easily observable.
ex.zh: 溫度的變化很容易觀察到。

ex.en: There was no observable difference between the two samples.
ex.zh: 兩個樣本之間看不出明顯的差異。

ex.en: No objector spoke up at the meeting, so the plan was approved.
ex.zh: 會議上沒有人提出異議，所以計畫通過了。

ex.en: A few objectors complained about the noise from the new road.
ex.zh: 少數反對者抱怨新馬路的噪音。

ex.en: The study was purely observational, so no one was given any treatment.
ex.zh: 這項研究純粹是觀察性的，所以沒有人接受任何治療。

ex.en: Observational skills are important for a good nurse.
ex.zh: 觀察能力對好護理師很重要。

ex.en: The obnoxious man talked loudly on the phone during the movie.
ex.zh: 那個討人厭的男人在電影放映時大聲講電話。

ex.en: Her obnoxious laugh annoyed everyone at the table.
ex.zh: 她那令人反感的笑聲讓同桌的人都很煩。

ex.en: The artist drew an oblique line across the page.
ex.zh: 畫家在紙上畫了一條斜線。

ex.en: The sun's oblique rays lit up the valley in the evening.
ex.zh: 傍晚斜射的陽光照亮了山谷。

ex.en: She made an oblique reference to his mistake.
ex.zh: 她委婉地暗示了他的錯誤。

ex.en: The minister gave an oblique answer instead of a direct yes or no.
ex.zh: 部長沒有直接回答是或不是，而是給了迂迴的答案。

ex.en: The teacher removed any objectionable language from the play.
ex.zh: 老師刪去了劇本中令人反感的用語。

ex.en: I found his jokes objectionable and left the room.
ex.zh: 我覺得他的笑話很令人反感，就離開了房間。

ex.en: A good map would obviate the need for a guide.
ex.zh: 有一張好地圖，就不需要嚮導了。

ex.en: The new system obviates the need to enter data by hand.
ex.zh: 新系統使手動輸入資料變得不必要。

ex.en: Don't obsess over small mistakes.
ex.zh: 別對小錯誤耿耿於懷。

ex.en: The idea began to obsess him, and he could not sleep.
ex.zh: 這個念頭開始困擾著他，讓他睡不著。

ex.en: The manager was obstructive and refused to share any information.
ex.zh: 那位經理處處阻撓，拒絕分享任何資訊。

ex.en: Some obstructive rules slowed down the whole project.
ex.zh: 有些礙手礙腳的規定拖慢了整個專案。

ex.en: An observant child noticed the small mistake on the sign.
ex.zh: 一個觀察入微的孩子發現了標示牌上的小錯誤。

ex.en: You have to be observant to be a good detective.
ex.zh: 要當個好偵探，就得觀察敏銳。

ex.en: He is an observant Jew who follows the traditions closely.
ex.zh: 他是嚴守教規的猶太人，遵循各項傳統。

ex.en: The family is very observant and goes to church every Sunday.
ex.zh: 這家人非常虔誠守教，每個星期日都去教堂。

ex.en: Her obstetrician said the baby was healthy.
ex.zh: 她的產科醫師說寶寶很健康。

ex.en: An obstetrician helped deliver the twins last night.
ex.zh: 昨晚一位產科醫師協助接生了那對雙胞胎。

ex.en: The dog sat down obediently when she called.
ex.zh: 她一叫，狗就乖乖坐下。

ex.en: The children obediently lined up at the door.
ex.zh: 孩子們乖乖地在門口排好隊。

ex.en: She plays the oboe in the school orchestra.
ex.zh: 她在學校管弦樂團裡吹雙簧管。

ex.en: The soft sound of the oboe filled the concert hall.
ex.zh: 雙簧管柔和的聲音充滿了音樂廳。

ex.en: He checked his phone obsessively all evening.
ex.zh: 他整個晚上都不停地查看手機。

ex.en: She cleaned the kitchen obsessively every night.
ex.zh: 她每晚都近乎強迫似地打掃廚房。

ex.en: He only referred to the problem obliquely, without naming anyone.
ex.zh: 他只是委婉地提到這個問題，沒有指名道姓。

ex.en: She answered the question obliquely to avoid an argument.
ex.zh: 她拐彎抹角地回答問題以避免爭吵。

ex.en: The sunlight fell obliquely through the window.
ex.zh: 陽光斜斜地從窗戶照進來。

ex.en: The path runs obliquely across the hill.
ex.zh: 那條小路斜斜地穿過山坡。

ex.en: He is too obstinate to listen to advice.
ex.zh: 他太固執，聽不進別人的建議。

ex.en: The obstinate child refused to eat his vegetables.
ex.zh: 那個倔強的孩子不肯吃蔬菜。

ex.en: The hotel staff were very obliging and carried our bags upstairs.
ex.zh: 旅館的員工非常樂意幫忙，還幫我們把行李搬上樓。

ex.en: He is an obliging neighbor who always lends us his tools.
ex.zh: 他是個樂於助人的鄰居，總是把工具借給我們。

ex.en: She decided to study obstetrics and become a doctor for pregnant women.
ex.zh: 她決定學產科，成為照顧孕婦的醫師。

ex.en: The hospital has a well-known obstetrics department.
ex.zh: 這家醫院有一個知名的產科。

ex.en: The bright sign looked obtrusive against the old stone wall.
ex.zh: 那面亮眼的招牌在古老石牆上顯得突兀。

ex.en: A good waiter is attentive but never obtrusive.
ex.zh: 好的服務生會周到但不令人覺得打擾。
